thread:
maria: 🚨 Getting alerts from us-west-2 egress — NAT gateway showing port usage spike and lots of connection_reset/timeout logs. App teams report increased 502/504 when talking to S3 and model-store.
jon: yup saw that. CloudWatch NAT:PortsUsed jumped from ~10k to 62k in ~3m. TCP TIME_WAIT and sockets in CLOSE_WAIT on node proxies.
siva: what are pod-side metrics? conn track? ephemeral range exhausted? any new deploys?
maria: no deploys at 2012 window. ss output from a busy node:
```
# ss -s
TCP:   12000 (estab 3000, closed 8500, orphaned 0, timewait 7000)

# sudo ss -tan | grep TIME-WAIT | wc -l
7000
```
alexa: looks like massive short-lived connections, likely model pulls or shard fanout. I see a concurrent model-get burst from many worker pods.
jon: prod model fetcher retries are aggressive on 429/504. We might be thundering herd-ing the NAT. Recommend throttling client concurrency and enable local caching.
siva: immediate mitigations we can try (quick wins):
- add egress route through a dedicated NAT instance pool (temporarily) to increase SNAT capacity
- enable tcp_tw_reuse and lower TIME_WAIT via sysctl on proxies
- adjust app to use keepalive + connection pooling
- add S3 VPC endpoint to bypass NAT for model pulls
maria: can someone run the quick sysctl on a canary proxy and watch for improvement? command:
```
sudo sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_tw_reuse=1
sudo sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_fin_timeout=30
```
jon: running on proxy-canary-3 now. will tail metrics. also spinning up a NAT instance group in us-west-2a to offload 30% of egress.
ops-bot: deploy job started: nat-instance-group/us-west-2a (ETA ~4m)
alexa: adding an iptables rule to keep established connections might help with conntrack churn. also consider increasing ip_local_port_range temporarily:
```
sudo sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range="15000 61000"
```
maria: good. App-side change: reduce parallel model fetchers per pod from 8 -> 2 and add jitter on retry.
jon: made a hotpatch to the fetcher config via feature-flag. rolling to 25% now.
deploy-bot: rollout 25% -> success. No errors in 120s.
siva: telemetry after sysctl + nat-instance up: PortsUsed down to ~28k, TIME_WAIT down to 2k on canary. Client 503s reduced by 70%.
maria: excellent. next steps:
- full rollout of fetcher throttle and keepalive in next 30m
- schedule S3 VPC endpoint and test model-store endpoint bypass (low risk)
- long term: egress pool per AZ + shared HTTP proxy with connection reuse OR deploy per-node local proxy to reduce SNAT fanout
- add alert for ephemeral port usage > 40k with runbook link
alexa: I'll open a follow-up RFC for egress architecture (proxy + VPC endpoints + autoscale NAT instances). Include cost estimate vs. dedicated NAT gateways.
jon: For postmortem, capture: root cause = concurrent model fetch retries + no pooling => ephemeral port exhaustion on NAT gateway; mitigations = patch client, sysctl knobs, temporary NAT instances, VPC endpoints.
maria: thumbs up. thanks for the rapid response :tada:
ops-bot: incident classified: severity=sev2, owner=maria, playbook=https://wiki.internal/egress-ports-playbook
maria: adding final note: keep an eye on other regions for same fingerprint. I'll loop in platform oncall to roll global mitigations.
